title: Canada PR Wait Times Ease but Citizenship Queue Nears 100,000 as Bill C-3 Demand Surges
excerpt: Processing times improve for key economic immigration programs while proof of citizenship applications more than double since eligibility expanded in December 2025.
body:
• Canada's July 7 processing times update shows permanent residence wait times dropping by one to two months across several economic immigration categories, including Canadian Experience Class and base Provincial Nominee Program applicants.
  • Proof of citizenship processing times surged to 19 months as the application queue neared 100,000 — more than doubling since Canada expanded citizenship-by-descent eligibility in December 2025.
  • IRCC will now publicly disclose how many permanent residence applications are waitlisted versus actively being processed, revealing that 40% of family sponsorship and 46% of protection applications are on hold.
  • Spousal sponsorship wait times continued climbing, with inland applications now at 27 months — more than double IRCC's 12-month service standard.

Canada's immigration department released updated processing times on July 7, delivering mixed news for the hundreds of thousands of applicants waiting for permanent residence and citizenship decisions.

PR Processing Times Ease for Key Economic Programs

Canadian Experience Class (CEC) applicants saw wait times fall from seven months to six, bringing processing within Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada's (IRCC) service standard for the first time in months. Base Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) applications also improved, dropping from 13 to 12 months, while Quebec Business Class wait times edged down by one month to 75 months.

https://x.com/CanadaImmigra20/status/2087171696142791156

The Federal Skilled Worker Program held steady at seven months, still a month above the six-month service standard. Express Entry-aligned PNP applications moved in the opposite direction, climbing from six to seven months.

The Atlantic Immigration Program's wait time remained flat at 26 months — more than double its 11-month service standard — while Start-up Visa and Self-Employed Persons Program applicants continue to face wait times exceeding 10 years.

Citizenship-by-Descent Queue Nears 100,000

The most dramatic shift came in proof of citizenship processing. The queue grew to 99,500 applicants as of July 7, an increase of roughly 17,500 in a single month. Processing times jumped to 19 months, up from 15 months in June's update.

The surge traces directly to Canada's December 2025 expansion of citizenship by descent under Bill C-3, which removed the first-generation limit for those born before that date. The change opened eligibility to anyone who can trace an unbroken line back to a Canadian ancestor, regardless of how many generations have passed. As recently as May, the queue stood at 70,400 with a 12-month wait.

"When we receive more applications for a program than there are spaces in the levels plan, some applications must wait until spaces become available in a future year."

— IRCC, updated application inventory webpage

An internal review of roughly 6,500 certificates already issued under Bill C-3 likely compounded the delays. IRCC paused finalizing new citizenship-by-descent applications in June while checking whether supporting documentation held up. The review concluded June 30, flagging 100 certificates for potentially insufficient documentation. Thirty-three were reinstated; the remaining 67 are still being resolved.

IRCC Opens Books on Waitlisted Applications

In a separate move on July 21, IRCC began publicly disclosing the proportion of permanent residence applications being actively processed versus those waitlisted due to insufficient admissions spaces under the 2026-2028 Immigration Levels Plan.

The first release, covering data through May 31, revealed a total of 705,315 permanent residence applications awaiting finalization. Under the Economic category, 75% of 238,335 applications were in active processing. Family applications fared worse: 40% of 159,765 were waitlisted. Protection applications had the highest waitlist rate at 46%, with 307,215 applications pending.

For 2026, the federal government plans to admit 380,000 permanent residents outside Quebec, including 239,800 through economic pathways and 84,000 through family reunification.

What This Means for NRI Applicants

For Indian nationals navigating Canadian immigration, the picture is nuanced. Express Entry applicants through CEC are seeing the system work closer to its intended timeline. But those on spousal sponsorship tracks face worsening delays — inland applications now take 27 months, up from 26, while Parents and Grandparents Program wait times eased to 30 months from 32.

Citizenship grant processing fell to 12 months, hitting its service standard, even as IRCC's citizenship grant inventory sits at 326,200 applications. Applicants considering proof of citizenship through descent face the stark math of a queue that has only grown month over month since Bill C-3 took effect. An application filed today likely won't see a decision until early 2028.
